paper.title_en: Measurement and analysis of the incomplete fusion strength function in the <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts></math>(<math><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mtext>lab</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>A</mi><mo>–</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> MeV)<math><mrow><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Te</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>130</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> system to probe entrance-channel dependence
paper.abstract_en: To investigate low-energy incomplete fusion (ICF) dynamics, the excitation functions (EFs) of different evaporation residues (ERs) produced in <math><mrow><mrow/><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mrow/><mmultiscripts><mi>Te</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>130</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> system were measured in the 4–7 MeV/nucleon energy range using the recoil-catcher activation technique followed by off-line <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray spectroscopy and analyzed in the framework of statistical model code pace4. It has been found that cross sections for <math><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> channels were well reproduced by the code, suggesting that they originate from complete fusion (CF) reactions. In contrast, the <math><mi>α</mi></math>-emitting channels display a marked enhancement over theoretical predictions, pointing to the contribution of incomplete fusion (ICF) processes arising from projectile breakup. To quantify these effects, the ICF fraction (<math><msub><mtext>F</mtext><mtext>ICF</mtext></msub></math>) has been deduced and analyzed as a function of projectile energy, mass asymmetry, Coulomb factor <math><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></math>, deformation parameter <math><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, and the <math><mi>α</mi></math>-separation energy of the projectile <math><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></math>. The results show that <math><msub><mtext>F</mtext><mtext>ICF</mtext></msub></math> increases with projectile energy and shows systematic dependence on mass asymmetry and <math><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></math>. However, comparisons with earlier studies reveal that these parameters alone are insufficient to fully account for the observed strength of ICF, underscoring the role of projectile structure and <math><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></math>. Additionally, the angular-momentum distributions calculated using ccfull indicate that, at the studied energies, both CF and ICF contributions arise from partial waves with <math><mrow><mi>ℓ</mi><mo><</mo><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>crit</mi></msub></mrow></math>, suggesting a diffused angular-momentum boundary rather than a sharp cutoff for the onset of ICF.
